records.region: Suriname; Commewijne and lower estuarine setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Provisional downstream receiving-river/system candidate. Original maps support the Tempati-to-Commewijne corridor and terminal setting, but not the complete selected southern opening.
records.material_pending_reason: The complete southernmost selected feeder and its connector into the mapped Tempati corridor remain unresolved in readable original cartography. Established downstream Tempati–Commewijne and Suriname estuarine correspondence does not close this initial gap.
material_pending_components: A permitted independent original map that shows the entire selected southern opening and connection into the upper Tempati at ordinary corridor scale.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected middle and lower route corresponds to the eastern Tempati branch, its junction with the separate Kleine Commewijne near Java, the northward Commewijne trunk past Stolkertsijver, and the westward lower river receiving Cottica before entering the Suriname estuary at Nieuw Amsterdam. The southernmost selected feeder and its full connection into the mapped Tempati remain insufficiently resolved. This is one source-material-pending record, not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.completion_scope: The selected middle and lower route corresponds to the eastern Tempati branch, its junction with the separate Kleine Commewijne near Java, the northward Commewijne trunk past Stolkertsijver, and the westward lower river receiving Cottica before entering the Suriname estuary at Nieuw Amsterdam. The southernmost selected feeder and its full connection into the mapped Tempati remain insufficiently resolved. This is one source-material-pending record, not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Provisional downstream receiving-river/system candidate. Original maps support the Tempati-to-Commewijne corridor and terminal setting, but not the complete selected southern opening.

component_scope_limits: The retained mainstem role does not make the selected Tempati reach uniformly Commewijne.
The 2018 project maps distinguish eastern Tempati Creek from western Little/Kleine Commewijne. Those western branches are not additional selected mainstems.

The 2013 Merian ESIA explicitly uses a different project naming convention: Commewijne for the wider branch often collectively called Tempati, and Tempati for a smaller project tributary. That convention is not a formal naming decision or a basis to erase the 2018 distinction.
Mapane and Cottica remain separate contributing branches, not aliases for the selected opening.

Brokopondo reservoir belongs to the separate Suriname corridor west of the mapped selected route. No reservoir passage is established on the mapped selected reach; the unresolved initial segment prevents a categorical whole-route statement.
The actual mapped receiving setting is the Suriname estuary. The retained sea-class endpoint is not extended into a selected open-Atlantic reach or treated as a surveyed mouth.
First-feeder name, exact headwater, hydronym transitions, current shorelines and formal registry status remain unassigned.

records.supported_name_scope: No river-name scope adopted. Land, glacier, lake, valley and fjord labels remain limited to their own feature types. Børglum River Formation in the geological legend is a stratigraphic-unit label, not evidence assigning a river name to the selected route.

completion_scope.scope_explanation: Completion concerns bounded direct reading of the complete selected geography and feature-type/name scope. It is not a claim that the modeled line is a mapped surface channel, subglacial drainage path, continuous hydraulic route, exact modern shoreline, or river mouth.

records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Every selected geographic component is covered by the retained Peary Land original. No representative or whole-route natural-river hydronym is established for the modeled ice/rock, lake/valley and fjord sequence. Completed terrain correspondence does not prove continuous surface or subglacial river flow.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected terminal belongs to the Jørgen Brønlund Fjord setting west of Kap Harald Moltke and north of the main Independence Fjord. Nearby Marie Sophie Gletscher and the separately mapped Inuiteq Sø are context, not alternate names or assumed traversals. Sheet 7 lies west of the target.

component_scope_limits: No river-name scope adopted. Land, glacier, lake, valley and fjord labels remain limited to their own feature types. Børglum River Formation in the geological legend is a stratigraphic-unit label, not evidence assigning a river name to the selected route.

records.region: Entre Ríos, Argentina; Gualeguaychú tributary and Río Uruguay receiving setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving/downstream river identity within the selected tributary system, not a uniform hydronym for the unnamed initial feeder.

actual_terminal.setting: Gualeguaychú tributary entrance into Río Uruguay beside Isla Lorenzo, downstream/east of Gualeguaychú city.
actual_terminal.stored_class_interpretation: Retained model metadata only; not evidence of an ocean mouth.

records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection begins on a small feeder near San Ernesto/Puntas del Gualeguaychú, joins the named Gualeguaychú corridor, and continues south past Gualeguaychú city before entering Río Uruguay. Original 1:250,000 and 1:100,000 cartography provide positive correspondence for the full single selected FID. Río Gualeguaychú is retained as representative identity only.
records.completion_scope: The selection begins on a small feeder near San Ernesto/Puntas del Gualeguaychú, joins the named Gualeguaychú corridor, and continues south past Gualeguaychú city before entering Río Uruguay. Original 1:250,000 and 1:100,000 cartography provide positive correspondence for the full single selected FID. Río Gualeguaychú is retained as representative identity only.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative selected river-system identity; tributary of Río Uruguay.

component_scope_limits: The selected small northwestern headward feeder is geographically covered but not independently named.
Gualeguaychú is the representative selected tributary identity; Río Uruguay is the separate receiving mainstem.
Named neighboring tributaries and floodplain channels are not relabelled Gualeguaychú.
No formal registry status, uniform whole-feature name, precise bank alignment, surveyed mouth point or present-day hydraulic behavior is established.

records.supported_name_scope: No name is assigned to this selected system. Regional maps distinguish the Boniface, Qikirtaluup Kuunga, Innuksuac and neighbouring lake settings, but those labels and basin surroundings do not establish a name for the complete selected route.
records.region: Northern Quebec, Canada; selected inland-to-coastal drainage.
records.material_pending_reason: The available regional originals do not distinguish the selected initial feeder, each middle lake/stream connection, material junction choices, the northern lower-route bend and the actual coastal outlet. No complete detailed companion map was acquired. These are genuine geographic source gaps, not a completed hydronym-scope hold.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
